title: GameFi Complete Guide
subtitle: Master Blockchain Gaming from Play-to-Earn to Advanced Strategies

intro.title: Introduction to GameFi
intro.content:
GameFi (Gaming + Finance) represents the convergence of blockchain technology and gaming, creating new economic models where players can truly own their in-game assets and earn real value from their gameplay. Unlike traditional games where your hard-earned items belong to the game company, GameFi puts ownership in your hands through NFTs and tokens.

In this comprehensive guide, you'll learn how blockchain gaming works, explore different game types from casual play-to-earn to fully on-chain games, understand gaming economics, and discover how players actually make money in GameFi. We'll cover major games like Axie Infinity and Gods Unchained, gaming infrastructure like Immutable and Ronin, and most importantly—the risks and sustainability factors you need to know.

game_types.title: Types of Blockchain Games
game_types.content: Blockchain games come in many forms, each with different economic models and gameplay mechanics. Understanding these categories helps you find games that match your goals and risk tolerance.

play_to_earn.title: Play-to-Earn (P2E) Games
play_to_earn.content:
Play-to-earn games reward players with cryptocurrency or NFTs for their time and skill. This model gained massive popularity in 2021 when Axie Infinity players in the Philippines were earning more than minimum wage by playing the game daily.

How P2E works:

  • Players complete quests, battles, or tasks to earn in-game tokens
  • These tokens can be sold on exchanges for real money
  • NFT items and characters can be traded on marketplaces
  • Player skill and time investment directly correlate with earnings

Popular P2E games:

  • Axie Infinity: Battle creatures called Axies, breed them, and earn SLP tokens
  • Pixels: Casual farming game on Ronin with relaxed gameplay
  • Big Time: Action RPG with tradeable NFT loot
  • Gods Unchained: Free-to-play trading card game

Reality check: Most P2E games have declining earnings as more players join. Early players often make the most money, while late entrants struggle to break even after purchasing entry NFTs.

move_to_earn.title: Move-to-Earn (M2E) Games
move_to_earn.content:
Move-to-earn games reward physical activity, typically using smartphone GPS and motion sensors to track movement. This category exploded in 2022 with STEPN, which at its peak had users earning $100+ per day for jogging.

How M2E works:

  • Purchase NFT sneakers or activity trackers
  • App tracks your walking, running, or other movement
  • Earn tokens based on distance, speed, and NFT attributes
  • Upgrade and trade NFTs for better earnings

Major M2E platforms:

  • STEPN: Running and walking app with sneaker NFTs (peaked at $4B+ market cap)
  • Sweat Economy: NEAR-based fitness rewards with lower entry cost
  • Genopets: Solana pet-raising game powered by your steps

Warning: M2E games are highly dependent on new user growth. When growth stops, token prices typically crash 90%+ as existing users sell their earnings. STEPN tokens fell from $4 to $0.20 in just 3 months.

fully_onchain.title: Fully On-Chain Games
fully_onchain.content:
Fully on-chain games store all game logic and state directly on the blockchain, not just assets. This creates truly unstoppable games that can survive even if the original developers disappear.

Why fully on-chain matters:

  • Permanence: The game exists on-chain forever
  • Composability: Other developers can build on top or create mods
  • True ownership: Not just assets, but the entire game state
  • Transparency: All game mechanics are verifiable code

Technical trade-offs:

  • Higher gas costs for every action
  • Slower gameplay due to block confirmation times
  • Limited complexity compared to traditional games
  • Usually require L2s or gaming chains for feasibility

Examples:

  • Pirate Nation: RPG on Apex (Arbitrum L3) with all state on-chain
  • Dark Forest: Space strategy game demonstrating zkSNARKs
  • Loot: Text-based RPG items that spawned an ecosystem

game_assets.title: Game Assets and Economics
game_assets.content: Understanding blockchain game assets is crucial for making informed decisions about which games to play and how to value items.

nfts.title: NFTs in Gaming
nfts.content:
NFTs in games represent unique items, characters, or land that you truly own. Unlike traditional games where the company can delete your account, NFTs persist on the blockchain.

Types of gaming NFTs:

  • Characters/Avatars: Axies, Gods Unchained cards, playable heroes
  • Equipment/Items: Weapons, armor, cosmetics
  • Land/Real Estate: Virtual plots in Sandbox, Decentraland
  • Consumables: Potions, crafting materials (often fungible)

NFT utility in games:

  • Gameplay access: Some games require NFT ownership to play
  • Enhanced earning: Higher-rarity NFTs often earn more rewards
  • Breeding/Crafting: Combine NFTs to create new ones
  • Governance: Vote on game development decisions

Trading and liquidity:

Gaming NFTs trade on specialized marketplaces like Immutable's marketplace, Fractal, or general platforms like OpenSea. Liquidity varies dramatically—popular game items trade instantly, while niche items may take weeks to sell.

Valuation factors:

  • Rarity (often from randomized attributes)
  • Earning potential in-game
  • Aesthetic appeal and status value
  • Game popularity and player count
  • Historical sales data and floor prices

tokens.title: Token Economics
tokens.content:
Most blockchain games use a dual-token model to separate governance from in-game earnings. Understanding this structure is critical for evaluating game sustainability.

Dual-token model (most common):

  • Governance token: Fixed supply, used for voting and staking (e.g., AXS, ILV, GMT)
  • In-game token: Unlimited or high-cap supply, earned through gameplay (e.g., SLP, GST)

Why dual tokens?

If gameplay directly earned the governance token, early players could extract all value before new players arrive. The in-game token acts as a buffer—it can be minted freely for rewards and has no governance value, protecting the main token.

Token sinks (crucial for sustainability):

Games need ways to remove tokens from circulation to prevent inflation:

  • Breeding costs (burn tokens to create new NFTs)
  • Upgrade/enhancement fees
  • Marketplace transaction fees
  • Crafting and repair costs

Warning signs of unsustainable tokenomics:

  • No meaningful token sinks
  • High daily inflation (>5% of circulating supply)
  • Most players are extracting value, few are adding
  • Token unlock schedules dumping on retail players

The death spiral:

When token rewards exceed token sinks, prices fall → earnings decrease → players leave → prices fall faster. This has killed dozens of P2E games. Successful games balance rewards with genuine token utility and sinks.

major_games.title: Major Blockchain Games
major_games.content: Let's examine the most significant blockchain games that have shaped the industry, analyzing what made them successful and what we can learn from their economics.

axie.title: Axie Infinity: The P2E Pioneer
axie.content:
Axie Infinity popularized play-to-earn gaming in 2021, reaching $4 billion in NFT trading volume and creating a scholarship economy in developing countries.

How Axie works:

  • Collect and battle creatures called Axies (each is an NFT)
  • Win battles to earn SLP (Smooth Love Potion) tokens
  • Breed Axies using AXS and SLP tokens to create new Axies
  • Trade Axies on marketplace, with rare ones worth thousands

Economic peak (2021):

  • Daily active users: 2.7 million
  • Average player earnings: $200-300/month in Philippines
  • AXS token: $160 all-time high
  • SLP token: $0.40 (from $0.01)

What went wrong:

Too many players earning SLP (40M+ daily) with insufficient sinks. Breeding costs couldn't absorb the flood of tokens. SLP crashed to $0.003, making gameplay unprofitable. The game shifted focus from earning to esports and land gameplay.

Lessons learned:

  • P2E can't sustain unlimited player growth
  • Token sinks must scale with player earnings
  • Games need fun gameplay, not just earning
  • Guild/scholarship model creates job opportunities but also extraction pressure

Current state:

Axie pivoted to Axie Infinity: Origins (free-to-play) and Axie Homeland (land gameplay). Focus shifted from P2E to competitive esports with the Ronin blockchain powering millions of daily transactions.

gods_unchained.title: Gods Unchained: Free-to-Play TCG
gods_unchained.content:
Gods Unchained is a trading card game that proves blockchain games can be genuinely fun while maintaining player ownership of cards.

Key features:

  • Free-to-play: No NFT purchase required to start
  • Earn cards by playing and ranking up
  • Cards become tradeable NFTs when you "forge" them
  • Competitive ranked play with weekend tournaments
  • Built on Immutable X for zero-fee trading

What makes it sustainable:

  • Focus on gameplay quality over P2E promises
  • Similar to Hearthstone—familiar to card game players
  • NFT cards have real utility (competitive advantage)
  • Revenue from card pack sales, not infinite token printing

Player earnings:

Modest and realistic. Top players earn hundreds by selling rare cards, but most players earn little to nothing. This is more sustainable than promises of daily earnings for everyone.

Challenges:

  • Lower liquidity than major games (smaller player base)
  • Card values fluctuate with game balance changes
  • Requires skill and time investment for competitive success

illuvium.title: Illuvium: AAA Open-World RPG
illuvium.content:
Illuvium aims to be the first AAA-quality blockchain game—an open-world RPG with stunning graphics and auto-battler mechanics.

Game mechanics:

  • Explore alien world, capture creatures (Illuvials)
  • Build teams for auto-battler combat
  • Craft items and equipment
  • Compete in ranked arena battles
  • Three interconnected games: Overworld, Arena, Zero

Economic model:

  • ILV token: Governance and staking rewards
  • sILV: In-game currency earned through gameplay
  • NFTs: Illuvials, land, equipment all tradeable

Built on Immutable X:

Zero gas fees for trading NFTs, important for a game with frequent item trades.

Current status:

Public beta launched in 2024 after years of development. High production values but slower player growth than expected, partly due to high PC requirements and complex onboarding.

Investment consideration:

Represents the high-budget, high-quality approach to blockchain gaming. Success depends on attracting mainstream gamers who care about gameplay quality over quick earning.

bigtime.title: Big Time: Action RPG
bigtime.content:
Big Time is a free-to-play multiplayer action RPG with time-traveling adventures and a unique approach to NFT integration.

Gameplay:

  • Hack-and-slash combat similar to Diablo
  • Team up with friends for dungeon runs
  • Collect cosmetics, weapons, and SPACE (in-game land NFTs)
  • Craft limited-edition items in your SPACE

Economic approach:

  • Free-to-play core game
  • NFT SPACE grants ability to craft/earn
  • Hourglass system regulates earning (NFT requires hourglasses to produce items)
  • BIGTIME token launched in late 2023

What's interesting:

Instead of pay-to-win or pure P2E, Big Time focuses on NFT cosmetics with status value and SPACE ownership for "production." This reduces pressure on token economics since not everyone needs to earn constantly.

Challenges:

  • High-end PC required for good performance
  • Learning curve for crypto-native features
  • Item saturation as more SPACE owners craft

infrastructure.title: Gaming Infrastructure
infrastructure.content: Blockchain games require specialized infrastructure—Ethereum mainnet is too slow and expensive for game transactions. Gaming-focused chains have emerged to solve this.

immutable.title: Immutable: zkEVM Gaming Platform
immutable.content:
Immutable provides infrastructure specifically designed for NFT games, combining zero gas fees with EVM compatibility.

Two solutions:

  • Immutable X: ZK-rollup with 9,000+ TPS, zero gas fees
  • Immutable zkEVM: EVM-compatible chain for more complex games

Developer benefits:

  • No gas fees for players (Immutable covers)
  • Fast transaction finality
  • Built-in marketplace and wallet infrastructure
  • SDKs for Unity, Unreal Engine

Major games:

Gods Unchained, Guild of Guardians, Illuvium, Ember Sword, and 200+ games in development.

IMX token:

Used for staking, governance, and paying protocol fees. Required holding for developers building on the platform.

ronin.title: Ronin: Ethereum Sidechain for Gaming
ronin.content:
Ronin was built by Sky Mavis specifically for Axie Infinity, then opened to other games. It's an Ethereum sidechain optimized for gaming transactions.

Key features:

  • Fast block times (3 seconds)
  • Low transaction fees (~$0.01-0.10)
  • Proof-of-Authority consensus (faster but more centralized)
  • Dedicated to gaming use cases

Major games:

Axie Infinity, Pixels, The Machines Arena, and growing ecosystem of casual games.

RON token:

Native token for gas fees and staking. Validators must stake RON to secure the network.

Security note:

Ronin suffered a $624M hack in 2022 when attackers compromised validator nodes. The team reimbursed users and improved security, but this highlights centralization risks in gaming chains.

gaming_l2s.title: Other Gaming L2s and Chains
gaming_l2s.content:
Beyond Immutable and Ronin, several chains target gaming as their primary use case:

Beam (Avalanche Subnet):

  • Avalanche subnet backed by Merit Circle DAO
  • Focus on AAA games and esports
  • Cheap transactions, fast finality

Xai (Arbitrum Orbit L3):

  • Gaming chain built as Arbitrum L3
  • Traditional gamers don't need wallets (account abstraction)
  • Backed by Offchain Labs

Treasure (Arbitrum):

  • Gaming ecosystem on Arbitrum
  • Shared liquidity and item marketplace
  • MAGIC token powers entire ecosystem

Why so many gaming chains?

Games need high throughput, low fees, and control over their economic environment. General-purpose L2s compete with DeFi for block space, while gaming chains prioritize game transactions.

guilds.title: Guilds and Scholarships
guilds.content: Gaming guilds emerged as a key part of the GameFi ecosystem, creating job opportunities in developing countries while raising questions about sustainability and labor practices.

ygg.title: Yield Guild Games (YGG)
ygg.content:
Yield Guild Games pioneered the scholarship model, where guilds purchase game assets and lend them to players in exchange for a share of earnings.

How YGG works:

  • Guild buys expensive game NFTs (Axies, land, etc.)
  • Scholars get access to play without upfront cost
  • Earnings split 60-70% to scholar, 30-40% to guild
  • Guild provides training and community support

YGG's investment approach:

  • Early investor in promising games
  • Build regional sub-DAOs (Southeast Asia, India, etc.)
  • Curate which games to support based on earning potential

Peak impact:

During Axie's prime, YGG scholars in Philippines earned more than local minimum wage. Thousands of families depended on scholarship income.

Current state:

With Axie earnings collapsed, YGG pivoted to Web3 gaming infrastructure and new games. The scholarship model works when games are profitable but creates dependency risks.

scholarship.title: The Scholarship Model
scholarship.content:
Benefits of scholarships:

  • Lower barriers to entry for players in developing countries
  • Risk on guild, not individual player
  • Community and training support
  • Diversification across multiple games

Criticisms and concerns:

  • Digital labor: Scholars work for below-minimum-wage rates in many cases
  • Extraction pressure: Guilds amplify selling pressure on game tokens
  • Unsustainability: Model requires constant growth or collapses
  • Centralization: A few large guilds control significant game assets

Other major guilds:

  • Merit Circle: DAO-governed guild with focus on competitive gaming
  • UniX Gaming: Data-driven approach to game selection
  • Good Games Guild: Regional focus on Asia-Pacific

Future of guilds:

As games shift from pure P2E to play-and-earn or free-to-play models, guilds are evolving into esports teams, game investors, and community organizers rather than pure scholarship providers.

earning.title: Earning Strategies in GameFi
earning.content: Let's get practical. How do people actually make money in blockchain games? Here are the main strategies, ranked from beginner to advanced.

playing.title: Earning Through Gameplay
playing.content:
Daily quest grinding:

Many P2E games reward daily quests or matches. Consistent players can earn modest amounts:

  • Time investment: 2-4 hours daily
  • Typical earnings: $50-200/month (varies hugely by game)
  • Requirements: Game NFTs (often $100-1000+ entry)

Competitive play:

Skilled players earn more through tournaments and ranked rewards:

  • Gods Unchained weekend tournaments: Prize cards worth $50-500
  • Axie leaderboard rewards: Top players earn thousands in AXS
  • Esports prizes: Growing but still small compared to traditional esports

Reality check on earnings:

Most P2E games follow this pattern:

  1. Early days: High earnings attract players
  2. Growth phase: Earnings diluted across more players
  3. Maturity: Only skilled or early players profit
  4. Decline: Most players earn below minimum wage

Sustainable approach:

Don't expect consistent income. Treat it as gaming with potential bonuses, not a job. Play games you enjoy, and view earnings as a nice extra.

trading.title: NFT Trading and Speculation
trading.content:
Trading game NFTs can be more profitable than playing, but requires different skills.

Flipping strategy:

  • Buy undervalued NFTs when game is out of favor
  • Sell during hype cycles or meta changes
  • Focus on functional items, not just cosmetics
  • Study game mechanics to identify valuable attributes

Successful trading examples:

  • Axie flippers who bought during bear market, sold during 2021 boom (10-50x gains)
  • Gods Unchained card speculators buying before meta shifts
  • Virtual land flippers in Sandbox, Decentraland

Trading tools:

  • Fractal, Immutable marketplace for game NFTs
  • OpenSea for general NFT trading
  • Game-specific marketplaces often have better liquidity

Risks:

  • Low liquidity—can't always sell when you want
  • Game updates can destroy item value overnight
  • Market manipulation by whales
  • Exit liquidity problem—who will buy from you?

Advanced strategy:

Some traders specialize in specific games, building deep knowledge of item values, meta changes, and player behavior. This is closer to professional trading than casual flipping.

breeding.title: Breeding and Creation
breeding.content:
Some games allow players to create new NFTs through breeding, crafting, or other creation mechanics. This can be profitable but requires capital and knowledge.

Breeding mechanics (Axie Infinity example):

  1. Own two compatible Axies (breeding parents)
  2. Pay breeding cost in AXS + SLP tokens
  3. Receive offspring with randomized traits from parents
  4. Sell offspring, hopefully for more than breeding cost

Profitability factors:

  • Parents' genetic traits (determines offspring value)
  • Current token prices (breeding cost changes)
  • Demand for specific traits or meta builds
  • Breeding count (Axies have limited breeding)

Other breeding/crafting games:

  • Pegaxy, ZED RUN (horse racing)
  • Crypto Unicorns (creature breeding)
  • Big Time (equipment crafting in SPACE)

The breeding trap:

When everyone breeds for profit, supply exceeds demand → prices crash → breeding becomes unprofitable. Successful breeders time the market or find niches (rare traits, competitive builds).

Advanced breeding:

Professional breeders track genetics, demand patterns, and token price cycles. Some make six figures, but it's closer to running a business than playing a game.

land.title: Virtual Land Ownership
land.content:
Virtual land in blockchain metaverses can generate passive income, but prices and utility vary dramatically.

How land generates value:

  • Rental income: Other players pay to use your land
  • Advertising/Sponsorships: Brands pay for high-traffic areas
  • In-game resources: Land produces materials or tokens
  • Development: Build games/experiences and charge admission

Major metaverse lands:

  • The Sandbox: Voxel metaverse, land sold in LAND NFTs
  • Decentraland: 3D virtual world with LAND parcels
  • Axie Infinity (Homeland): Land gameplay producing resources
  • Ember Sword: MMORPG with land ownership

Land prices:

Highly variable. Prime locations near popular areas: $10,000-100,000+. Remote parcels: $100-1,000. Prices rose dramatically in 2021-2022 hype, then crashed 70-90%.

Reality of land income:

Most virtual land generates zero income. Only highly developed parcels with real traffic earn meaningful returns. It's more like speculative real estate than passive income.

Success factors:

  • Location near popular attractions
  • Active development and events
  • Marketing to drive visitors
  • Partnerships with brands or creators

Investment perspective:

Virtual land is a bet on the metaverse's future. If millions eventually "live" in these worlds, prime land could be valuable. If they don't, it's worthless. High risk, long time horizon.

risks.title: Risks and Sustainability
risks.content: GameFi's biggest challenge is sustainability. Many games promise earnings but lack economic models that can support them long-term. Understanding these risks is crucial before investing time or money.

sustainability.title: Economic Sustainability
sustainability.content:
For a P2E game to be sustainable, value must flow IN faster than it flows OUT. When players extract more value than new money enters, the game economy collapses.

The fundamental equation:

Sustainable game = (New player deposits + Marketplace fees + Sponsorships) > (Player withdrawals + Development costs)

Why most P2E games fail:

  • Too much focus on earning: Players join only to extract value
  • Insufficient value creation: No real product or entertainment value
  • Pyramid dynamics: Early players profit from late entrants
  • No sustainable revenue: Token sales can't fund rewards forever

Sustainable models exist:

  • Genuine entertainment value: Players pay because it's fun (Gods Unchained)
  • Cosmetic sales: Optional NFT purchases fund development (Big Time)
  • Competitive ecosystems: Players invest to gain advantage (esports)
  • Creator economies: Users build content that attracts others (Sandbox)

What to look for:

  • Would people play this game without earning?
  • Is there a clear revenue source beyond token sales?
  • Do token sinks scale with player growth?
  • Are developers transparent about economics?

death_spiral.title: Game Death Spirals
death_spiral.content:
Many GameFi projects follow a predictable death spiral pattern. Understanding this helps you avoid being exit liquidity.

The typical death spiral:

  1. Launch hype: High APYs attract initial players
  2. Growth phase: Token price rises, media coverage increases
  3. Peak: Maximum players, highest earnings, most hype
  4. Oversaturation: Too many players earning, not enough new deposits
  5. Price decline: Token rewards become worth less
  6. Player exodus: Unprofitable players leave, selling assets
  7. Collapse: Remaining players can't sell, game becomes ghost town

Real examples:

  • Axie Infinity SLP: $0.40 → $0.003 (99% drop) over 6 months
  • STEPN GST: $8 → $0.01 (99.8% drop) over 3 months
  • DeFi Kingdoms JEWEL: $20 → $0.10 (95% drop)

Warning signs you're in a death spiral:

  • Declining daily active users
  • Token price falling despite high APY promises
  • Community complaints about earnings
  • Developers promising "upcoming features" without delivery
  • New player growth slowing

How to avoid being exit liquidity:

  • Don't buy at peak hype
  • Withdraw earnings regularly, don't compound endlessly
  • Monitor player growth trends
  • Have an exit strategy before entering
  • Don't fall for sunk cost fallacy

regulatory.title: Regulatory Risks
regulatory.content:
GameFi exists in a legal gray area. Play-to-earn mechanics may be considered gambling, securities, or unlicensed money transmission in some jurisdictions.

Regulatory concerns:

  • Gambling laws: Games with randomized rewards might be gambling
  • Securities laws: Tokens promising returns could be securities
  • Labor laws: Are scholarship players employees?
  • Tax implications: Earnings are taxable income in most countries

Regional restrictions:

Several countries have restricted or banned blockchain games:

  • China banned crypto gaming entirely
  • South Korea restricts P2E games
  • Several countries require gambling licenses for random rewards

Project risks:

  • Developers might face legal action
  • Games could be forced to shut down in certain regions
  • Bank accounts and payment processors might get frozen

Player protection:

  • Understand local tax obligations (often 15-40% of earnings)
  • Keep records of all transactions
  • Be aware games might disappear suddenly
  • Don't invest more than you can afford to lose

evaluation.title: Smart Game Evaluation
evaluation.content:
Before investing time or money in any blockchain game, evaluate it critically:

Game quality checklist:

  • Is the gameplay actually fun without earning?
  • Are graphics and mechanics up to modern standards?
  • Is there a roadmap with realistic milestones?
  • Has the team delivered on past promises?

Economic model checklist:

  • What are the token sources (emissions) and sinks (burning)?
  • Is there a clear path to sustainability?
  • What's the entry cost and estimated payback time?
  • How sensitive are earnings to player count changes?

Team and community:

  • Is the team public and experienced?
  • Track record in gaming or crypto?
  • Active development and communication?
  • Community sentiment (Discord, Twitter)?

Market metrics:

  • Daily active users (growing or declining?)
  • Token price trends (stable, rising, or crashing?)
  • NFT floor prices and trading volume
  • Marketplace liquidity (can you actually sell?)

Red flags to avoid:

  • Anonymous team
  • Unrealistic APY promises (1000%+)
  • No working product, just whitepaper
  • Heavy marketing, light on substance
  • Copied gameplay from other games
  • Locked liquidity that team can access
  • Token unlocks dumping on retail

Final advice:

Approach GameFi with skepticism and curiosity. The technology enables genuine innovation in game ownership and economies, but most projects are unsustainable cash grabs. Play games you enjoy, treat any earnings as bonuses, and never invest more than you can afford to lose.

play_to_earn.definition: Gaming model where players earn cryptocurrency or NFTs through gameplay. Players invest time and skill to generate real income, though sustainability varies widely by game.

game_nft.definition: Non-fungible tokens representing in-game assets like characters, items, or land. Unlike traditional games, players truly own these assets and can trade them on open markets.

in_game_token.definition: Cryptocurrency earned through gameplay, typically with unlimited or high supply. Often paired with a governance token in dual-token models. Value depends on game health and token sinks.

guild.definition: Organization that purchases game assets (NFTs) and lends them to players (scholars) in exchange for a share of earnings. Pioneered by Yield Guild Games during Axie Infinity's peak.

scholarship.definition: Arrangement where a guild or investor lends game NFTs to a player who doesn't have capital to buy them. Earnings are split between scholar and sponsor, typically 60-70% to scholar.

fully_onchain.definition: Game where all logic and state are stored on the blockchain, not just assets. These games are truly decentralized and can survive without the original developers.

gaming_l2.definition: Layer 2 solution or dedicated blockchain optimized for gaming transactions. Features fast speeds, low fees, and high throughput needed for game actions. Examples: Immutable, Ronin, Beam.

breeding.definition: Mechanic where players combine two NFTs (usually creatures) and pay tokens to create a new NFT with traits from both parents. Can be profitable but requires understanding genetics and market demand.

land.definition: NFT representing ownership of space in a blockchain metaverse. Can potentially generate income through rental, resource production, or hosting events. Highly speculative asset class.

game_economy.definition: The economic system of a blockchain game, including token emissions (rewards), sinks (burning mechanisms), NFT markets, and value flows. Healthy economies balance earning with spending.
